name: Domains of Shabbat (Reshuyot)
notes: Classification of public domain (reshut harabim), private domain (reshut hayachid), karmelit, and exempt domain (mekom patur) for purposes of Shabbat carrying prohibitions

name: Pre-Shabbat Activities (Erev Shabbat Restrictions)
notes: Restrictions on beginning activities on Shabbat eve that will continue into Shabbat, including the Beit Shammai/Beit Hillel dispute about when one must cease

name: Shabbat Candles (Hadlakat Nerot Shabbat)
notes: Laws of kindling Shabbat lights, permitted and forbidden wicks and oils, and the obligation to light before Shabbat

name: Hatmanah (Insulating Food on Shabbat)
notes: Laws of insulating cooked food before Shabbat to keep it warm, including permitted and forbidden insulating materials and heat-generating vs. non-heat-generating materials

name: Bishul on Shabbat (Cooking Prohibition)
notes: Laws of the prohibition of cooking on Shabbat including chazarah (returning food to the fire), kli rishon/sheni, and related rabbinic decrees

name: Chazarah (Returning Food to Heat on Shabbat)
notes: Laws regarding returning a pot to the stove on Shabbat, and the conditions under which it is permitted

name: Medical Treatment on Shabbat (Refuah b'Shabbat)
notes: Rabbinic prohibition on taking medicine or engaging in medical treatments on Shabbat unless there is danger to life, including specific cases of foods and ointments used medicinally

name: Pikuach Nefesh (Life-Threatening Danger Overrides Shabbat)
notes: The principle that saving life overrides Shabbat, including childbirth, circumcision complications, and related cases

name: Measures for Carrying on Shabbat (Shi'urei Hotzaah)
notes: The minimum measures of various substances for which one becomes liable for carrying in a prohibited domain on Shabbat

name: Thirty-Nine Melachot (Arba'im Chaser Achat)
notes: The enumerated list of the 39 primary categories of prohibited labor on Shabbat derived from the work of the Tabernacle

name: Sin-Offerings for Shabbat Violations
notes: Rules determining how many sin-offerings one must bring for multiple Shabbat violations, based on awareness, categories of labor, and number of Shabbatot

name: Throwing Objects on Shabbat (Zrikah)
notes: Laws of liability for throwing objects between domains on Shabbat, including objects that pass through a public domain between two private domains

name: Tying and Untying Knots on Shabbat (Kesher v'Hitarah)
notes: Laws of the prohibited labors of tying and untying on Shabbat, including which knots are Torah-level prohibitions and which are rabbinic

name: Trapping on Shabbat (Tzeidah)
notes: Laws of the prohibited labor of trapping animals on Shabbat, including minimum enclosure sizes for liability and distinction between domesticated and wild animals

name: Writing on Shabbat (Ketivah)
notes: Laws of the prohibited labor of writing two letters on Shabbat, including valid writing substances, languages, and surfaces

name: Building on Shabbat (Binyan)
notes: Laws of the prohibited labor of building on Shabbat, including any constructive act that endures

name: Weaving on Shabbat (Oreg)
notes: Laws of the prohibited labors of weaving, making meshes, sewing, and tearing on Shabbat including minimum measures for liability

name: Extinguishing Fire on Shabbat (Mechabeh)
notes: Laws of extinguishing fire on Shabbat, exemptions for fear and the sick, and indirect extinguishing

name: Preventing Fire Spread on Shabbat
notes: Laws of rescuing items from a fire on Shabbat, how much one may rescue, use of barriers, and role of gentile firefighters

name: Rescuing Sacred Writings from Fire on Shabbat
notes: The obligation and limits of rescuing Torah scrolls, Prophets, Writings, and their coverings from fire on Shabbat

name: What Animals May Carry on Shabbat
notes: Detailed laws of what equipment and adornments animals may go out with into the public domain on Shabbat, distinguishing protective items from burdens

name: Women's Ornaments on Shabbat
notes: Laws of which ornaments and accessories a woman may wear into the public domain on Shabbat and which are considered burdens

name: Circumcision Overriding Shabbat
notes: Laws of how circumcision at its appointed time overrides Shabbat, what preparations may be made on Shabbat, and when the override applies

name: Timing of Circumcision (Zman Milah)
notes: Laws governing when circumcision is performed — eighth day, ninth, tenth, eleventh, or twelfth day — based on birth circumstances, illness, and Shabbat/Festival coincidence

name: Shreds that Invalidate Circumcision (Tzitzin HaMeakvin)
notes: Which remaining flesh shreds invalidate a circumcision and require correction, and the requirement to uncover the corona membrane (priah)

name: Childbirth on Shabbat
notes: Laws permitting desecration of Shabbat for a woman giving birth, calling a midwife, and related actions

name: Preparation of a Corpse on Shabbat
notes: What may and may not be done for a corpse on Shabbat, including anointing, rinsing, moving limbs, and closing eyes

name: Types of Muktzeh (Categories)
notes: Different categories of muktzeh including muktzeh machmat gufo, muktzeh machmat chisaron kis, and graf shel re'i (disgusting objects set aside from use)

name: Prohibition of Weekday Speech on Shabbat (Dibur b'Shabbat)
notes: Prohibition against discussing weekday activities such as hiring workers or commercial arrangements on Shabbat

name: Gentile Performing Labor on Shabbat (Amirah l'Nochri)
notes: Laws regarding instructing or benefiting from a gentile's performance of prohibited labor on Shabbat, including the cases of a lamp lit by a gentile and a ramp made by a gentile

name: Training Minors in Shabbat Observance (Chinuch)
notes: The obligation of parents to prevent children from desecrating Shabbat even though minors are not obligated, as derived from Mishnah Shabbat chapter 16

name: Filtering and Selecting on Shabbat (Borer)
notes: Laws of the prohibited labor of selecting on Shabbat, including filtering wine, separating chaff from grain, and similar activities

name: Squeezing Fruits on Shabbat (Sechitah)
notes: Laws of squeezing fruits for their juice on Shabbat and the status of liquids that seep from fruit on their own

name: Folding Garments on Shabbat
notes: Laws permitting folding garments on Shabbat for use on Shabbat, and prohibiting folding in preparation for after Shabbat

name: Annulling Vows on Shabbat
notes: Permission to nullify or dissolve vows on Shabbat when the vow affects Shabbat observance or oneg Shabbat

name: Measuring on Shabbat
notes: Prohibition of measuring on Shabbat and exceptions for measuring a mikveh, a rag for ritual impurity, or for a mitzva purpose

name: Eighteen Decrees of Beit Shammai
notes: The eighteen rabbinic decrees issued by Beit Shammai's majority in the upper story of Chananya ben Chizkiya ben Garon, representing a landmark moment in rabbinic legislation

name: Ways of the Amorite (Darkei haEmori)
notes: Prohibition of superstitious practices associated with gentile customs, such as using a fox's tooth or a crucifixion nail as a remedy

name: Primary and Secondary Vessels (Kli Rishon v'Sheni)
notes: Distinction between a primary vessel that was on the fire and a secondary vessel into which food was poured, affecting cooking prohibition on Shabbat

name: Incomplete Labor Performed by Two People (Shenayim she'Asu)
notes: The rule that when two people jointly perform a prohibited labor, each performing only part, they are generally exempt, and its exceptions

name: Unusual Manner of Performing Labor on Shabbat (Shinui)
notes: The principle that performing a prohibited labor on Shabbat in an unusual manner (shinui) affects liability, including cases of carrying behind one's back

name: Borrowing and Lending on Shabbat
notes: Laws permitting informal borrowing of food or vessels on Shabbat using euphemistic language to avoid commercial transactions

name: Drawing Lots on Shabbat
notes: Permission to draw lots among family members for food portions on Shabbat, and among priests for sacrificial portions on Festivals

name: Waiting at Techum Boundary on Shabbat Eve
notes: Law of waiting at the Shabbat boundary at nightfall in order to tend to needs immediately after Shabbat, including permitted and forbidden purposes

name: Funeral Preparations at Shabbat's End
notes: Laws of waiting at the Shabbat boundary to attend to funeral needs, and use of items prepared by gentiles (coffin, grave) on Shabbat for a Jew

name: Eight Sheratzim (Specific Creeping Animals with Impurity)
notes: The eight specific creeping animals listed in Leviticus 11 that transmit ritual impurity, distinct from other creeping animals

name: Idolatry's Impurity by Carrying (Tum'at Masa of Avodah Zarah)
notes: The derivation that idolatrous objects transmit impurity by carrying (like a menstruating woman) even without direct contact, derived from Isaiah 30:22

name: Casting Lots for Priestly Portions on Festivals
notes: The permissibility of casting lots among priests for sanctified foods on Festivals but not for specific portions

name: Diverse Species in a Garden Bed (Arugah)
notes: The rule permitting five different species in a six-by-six handbreadth garden bed, one in each corner and one in the center, without violating kilayim

name: Duration of Semen's Impurity (Three Days)
notes: The derivation that a woman who discharges semen within three days of relations is ritually impure, based on the verse from Exodus 19:15

name: Smearing Oil as Substitute for Drinking on Yom Kippur
notes: The derivation that anointing/smearing oil is prohibited on Yom Kippur like drinking, based on Psalms 109:18

name: Perforated and Unperforated Flowerpots (Atzitz Nakuv)
notes: The distinction between a perforated flowerpot (treated as connected to the ground) and unperforated pot for purposes of agricultural laws and Shabbat picking prohibition

name: Folk Remedies and Superstitious Cures
notes: Items used as folk remedies such as locust eggs, fox teeth, and nails from the crucified — Rabbi Meir permits, Rabbis prohibit as darkei haEmori

name: Flutes at a Funeral on Shabbat
notes: Prohibition on a Jew using flutes brought by a gentile on Shabbat for a funeral eulogy unless they were brought from within the techum

name: Coffin and Grave Made by Gentile on Shabbat
notes: A coffin or grave made by a gentile on Shabbat: if done for himself, a Jew may use it; if done for a Jew, it is permanently forbidden
